# 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 378r

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** David consulted with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader. **2** And David said to all the assembly of Israel, "If it seems good to you and if it is the will of the LORD our God, let us send word far and wide to the rest of our brothers throughout all the lands of Israel, and also to the priests and Levites in their cities and pasturelands, that they may be gathered to us. **3** Then let us bring back the ark of our God to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul."

**4** All the assembly agreed to do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people. **5** So David assembled all Israel, from the Shihor of Egypt to Lebo-hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim. **6** And David and all Israel went up to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath-jearim that belongs to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the LORD, who is enthroned above the cherubim, where his name is invoked.

**7** They carried the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, and Uzzah and Ahio were driving the cart. **8** David and all Israel were celebrating before God with all their might, with songs, lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.

**9** When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzzah put out his hand to steady the ark, for the oxen had stumbled. **10** And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah, and he struck him down because he had put out his hand to the ark, and he died there before God.

**11** David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah. And that place is called Perez-uzzah to this day. **12** And David was afraid of God that day, and he said, "How can I bring the ark of God home to me?"

**13** So David did not take the ark home into the city of David, but took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. **14** The ark of God remained with the household of Obed-edom, in his house, for three months. And the LORD blessed the household of Obed-edom and all that he had.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter is the first half of a deliberate diptych (ch. 13 / ch. 15): the wrong way and the right way to bring the ark. The Chronicler inserts the consultative assembly scene (vv.1-4) — absent from 2 Samuel 6 — to show that the failure was not one of communal will but of procedural knowledge. The *ma'al* theme from chapter 10 recurs implicitly: Uzzah's death, like Saul's, results from improper approach to holy things. The narrative arc from anger (v.11) to fear (v.12) to blessing (v.14) will resolve in chapter 15 when David discovers the Levitical ordinance. The threshing floor — a place of grain processing — becomes a place of divine judgment, a pattern that will culminate in 2 Chronicles 3:1 where the temple is built on a threshing floor.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.4 — Assembly's response
- **EMET:** "all the-assembly to-do so, for the-thing [was] right in-the-eyes of-all the-people"
- **LOGOS:** "All the assembly agreed to do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people"
- **PNEUMA:** "The whole assembly enthusiastically agreed, because everyone saw that it was the right thing to do"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS wording adopted. PNEUMA's "enthusiastically" is not in the Hebrew text.

### V.8 — "celebrating" intensity
- **EMET:** "celebrating [mesachakim] before God with-all strength"
- **LOGOS:** "celebrating before God with all their might"
- **PNEUMA:** "celebrated wildly before God, singing with all their might"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "celebrating before God with all their might" — PNEUMA's "wildly" adds a connotation of disorder not present in the Hebrew *mesachakim* (playing/celebrating).

### V.10 — Manner of death
- **EMET:** "and-he-struck-him because he-put-forth his-hand upon the-ark, and-he-died there before God"
- **LOGOS:** "he struck him down because he had put out his hand to the ark, and he died there before God"
- **PNEUMA:** "God struck him dead on the spot — because he had touched the ark. He died right there in God's presence."
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS wording adopted. PNEUMA's "on the spot" and dash-separated clause add dramatic emphasis beyond the Hebrew's terse report.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
